description: Representing the Instituto Tecnológico de Chihuahua (ITCH) in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our multidisciplinary team unites diverse technical expertise driven by a profound sense of responsibility toward wildfire management.
summary: We developed Choki, a geospatial intelligence web platform that, for the first time, reconstructs a continuous, clean, and harmonized historical time series of forest fires from 2000 to 2026 by fusing data from the MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. Our platform addresses one of the most significant issues encountered in the European Union in 2025. Analyses based on satellite data from the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) revealed that 1,079,538 hectares—an area roughly equivalent to the size of Cyprus—were devastated by fire across several EU countries. Currently, analyzing the actual long-term progression of fires is imprecise: historical records contain methodological gaps between sensors, false negatives caused by cloud cover, and false alarms triggered by solar reflections or industrial activity. The NASA FIRMS application uses data from both VIIRS and MODIS with a 1 km threshold, which results in duplicate, unusable information. To unify this data, we apply the Haversine formula for spherical distance along with a dynamic geometry rule (d ≤ ri + rj +δ).
details:
What does it do, and how does it work?

  • It combines over 20 years of thermal detections from MODIS (2006–present) and VIIRS (2012–present) into a unified timeline, avoiding data duplication.
  • It provides actionable information through interactive, color-coded calendars and spatial animations.
  • It employs machine learning —specifically neural networks— to analyze patterns and construct a mathematical model based on the Haversine formula for spherical distance.

How does it work?

  1. Multi-Sensor Ingestion: Loads historical archives and near-real-time (NRT) data from NASA FIRMS (MCD14ML, MCD14DL, VNP14IMGML, VJ114IMGML, VJ214IMGML) in 5-day chunks, normalizing confidence levels, satellite identifiers, and pixel scan * track footprint geometry via Pydantic v2 schemas.
  2. Spatial Indexing: Stores records in SQLite backed by a native R-Tree spatial index (hotspots_rtree) for sub-second bounding-box and polygon queries.
  3. Dynamic Co-Location & Calibration: Groups detections within the spherical Haversine footprint rule (d≤ri+rj+δ) and time window of 180 minutes into unique thermal_events, preventing MODIS/VIIRS double counting.
  4. Statistical & Neural Audit: Computes historical fire fingerprints, monthly burning calendars, Z-MAD anomaly classification, and Theil-Sen trend slopes. Includes custom-built neural networks (TinyFireTransformer with 2-head self-attention + GELU and VerifierNetGatedResMLP with GLU residual blocks inside DualFireEnsemble).
  5. Interactive Visualization & Export: Serves an interactive web interface (HTML5/CSS3/JS + React 18.3.1 + PWA Service Worker) featuring color-coded burning calendars, spatial playback animations, and downloadable CSV and RFC 7946 GeoJSON reports.

What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates cross-sensor inflation when comparing pre-2012 MODIS records with post-2012 VIIRS observations.
  • Accelerates ecological risk analysis for researchers, civil protection agencies, and environmental planners.
  • Runs self-contained on standard local hardware without heavy external GIS database servers.

What do you hope to achieve?

  • Provide a reproducible, transparent baseline to measure long-term wildfire trends across vulnerable regions—such as the EU regions impacted in 2025—free from sensor-transition artifacts and at the same time, democratize access to harmonized NASA FIRMS thermal data through an intuitive calendar, map, and export interface.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Development Tools: Antigravity, Python standard tooling, Git
  • Infrastructure & Technological Hosting Target hosting: Amazon Web Services (AWS) (deployment manifests not yet included in this repository); Local HTTP runtime via server.py (ThreadingHTTPServer on port 8766).
  • Backend & API Python: (server.py, pipeline/*, scripts/*) and C++ (declared in project stack; native C execution in repo is provided via SQLite R-Tree spatial engine, with no standalone .cpp files currently committed).
  • Frontend & UI: HTML5, JavaScript (ES6+), CSS3, React 18.3.1 (web/vendor/ + web/js/choki-react.js), html2canvas 1.4.1, PWA Manifest & Service Worker (web/manifest.webmanifest, web/sw.js).
  • Programming Languages: Python (3.14.10 verified), JavaScript, HTML, CSS (C++ in declared project profile).
  • AI & Machine Learning: Pure-Python custom autograd (MicroValue), TinyFireTransformer (2-head self-attention + GELU), VerifierNetGatedResMLP (GLU ResBlocks), and DualFireEnsemble in pipeline/choki_ai.py
  • Data Processing & Geospatial: Python (numpy 2.5.4, orjson 3.13.0, pydantic 2.14.2, sqlite3 3.54.0 R-Tree), Haversine dynamic geometry, Theil-Sen slope, Z-MAD anomaly scoring, GeoJSON RFC 7946.
  • Async Tasks & Caching: Python background daemon thread (_start_nrt_auto_sync_loop(900) in server.py), gzip compression, ETag HTTP caching, PWA Service Worker cache (web/sw.js).
  • Software & Design: HTML5, CSS3, React, SVG branding (web/assets/logo/project-logo.svg).
